hero.title: I build products like they’re my business.
hero.subtitle: Product entrepreneur · AI builder · Professor · Advisor
hero.description: I decide what to build, why it matters, and how to make it real — from AI workers at InfiniteWatch to ventures at HuTech, with a decade of hard-earned lessons across fintech, data, hardware, and emerging markets.

about.title: Product entrepreneurship, assembled
about.subtitle: The title is optional. The ownership is not.
about.quote: Product entrepreneurship isn’t founding a company. It’s owning a product like it’s your business — and being the one whose stomach drops when the number doesn’t move.
about.paragraph1: Nobody handed me a playbook. I assembled this craft from two schools and a decade of companies. IE gave me business, data, and systems fluency. LEINN gave me entrepreneurship in the only format that sticks: real teams, real projects, real money on the line.
about.paragraph2: Eight companies supplied the rest of the muscle: freedom at Kibber, direction at Karmacracy, taste at Ibil, wings at MainTool, customer obsession at Graphext, leadership and scale at CoverWallet, and experimental humility in payments across Africa at KingMakers.
about.paragraph3: Today I’m betting the whole pile on the frontier: building AI workers at InfiniteWatch, advising venture building at HuTech, and teaching at NYU Stern. I didn’t get promoted into being a product entrepreneur. I built one out of myself — and never waited for permission.

journey.title: The making of a product entrepreneur

spark.title: Start with permission
spark.subtitle: Kibber · Freedom
spark.description: Ownership starts as permission you give yourself: the right to have an opinion, try, fail, and choose a direction before anyone gives you the title.

foundation.title: Point at the problem
foundation.subtitle: Karmacracy · Direction
foundation.description: Freedom without direction is just wandering with confidence. The entrepreneur’s first job is to choose a problem worth solving and say why it matters before writing a spec.
foundation.detailed: A product without a why is just features in a trench coat.

summit.title: Learn the no
summit.subtitle: Ibil · Taste
summit.description: Half of product judgment is knowing what to refuse: the feature, customer, or shortcut you will not take. Taste is mostly subtraction.

leadership.title: Earn your wings
leadership.subtitle: MainTool · Hardware, marketing, voice
leadership.description: Innovation is a process you run on purpose. Hardware taught me to make it physical, marketing taught me to write the words myself, and speaking taught me to carry the story out loud.

mission.title: Make it matter
mission.subtitle: Graphext · CoverWallet · KingMakers
mission.description: A product does not exist until someone succeeds with it. Customer value, organizational leadership, domain depth, and experiments across Africa turned craft into responsibility at scale.

vision.title: Bet on the frontier
vision.subtitle: InfiniteWatch · AI workers
vision.description: Now every muscle fires at once: freedom to bet, direction to aim, taste to refuse, ownership to carry it, and the humility to let evidence change your mind.

lanEgitea.application: Treat the product like your business. Carry the number, the trade-offs, and the consequences.

gardentasuna.application: Make the problem, the bet, and the evidence visible before asking a team to build.

auzolan.application: Leadership is moving an idea through a real organization, with its gravity, politics, and constraints.

slowDown.name: Experiment honestly
slowDown.description: Bet, measure, kill what is wrong, and double down on what works. Hold every idea loosely enough for evidence to change it.

backwardThinking.name: Start from success
backwardThinking.description: Work backwards from the moment a real customer succeeds, then build the system that makes that moment repeatable.

mission.title: The evidence

foodie.label: Featured Build Case
foodie.title: Gipuzkoa Foodie
foodie.subtitle: A curated restaurant guide built as a full-stack local discovery product for Gipuzkoa.
foodie.description: Gipuzkoa Foodie is a bilingual food discovery experience that turns local restaurant curation into a usable digital product. I built it with a modern React frontend and a dedicated API/backend setup so the experience could scale beyond a static directory.
foodie.outcome: The project combines editorial curation, product thinking, and practical engineering: category-based exploration, paginated restaurant discovery, locale-aware content, and an operational path to keep restaurant data fresh through a structured import workflow.

bullets.one: React + TypeScript frontend with Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui, deployed as a Cloudflare static app.
bullets.two: Express + Prisma API with PostgreSQL on Railway, designed to support categories, restaurants, and locale-aware responses.
bullets.three: Content operations workflow that can seed restaurant data from structured Notion exports into the production database.

digest.label: Featured Build Case
digest.title: Product Digest
digest.subtitle: A medium-style product publication and operating system for daily PM writing, editorial workflow, and scheduled publishing.
digest.description: Product Digest is more than a content site. I built it as a product knowledge hub where editorial publishing, search, subscriptions, and publishing automation work together as one operating system for product thinking.
digest.outcome: The project blends editorial UX with production-grade publishing infrastructure: Next.js + MDX for the reading experience, PostgreSQL-backed scheduled publishing, a Railway API for subscriptions and content operations, and Cloudflare Workers Cron to automate publishing on a recurring schedule.

bullets.one: Next.js + TypeScript frontend with MDX-driven publishing, search index generation, RSS, sitemap, and a publication-style reading experience.
bullets.two: Database-backed publishing model where scheduled and published posts live in PostgreSQL and can be synced, updated, and released programmatically.
bullets.three: Cloudflare deployment with OpenNext plus a Cloudflare Worker scheduler that triggers due-post publication through a protected backend API.

newsgang.label: Featured Build Case
newsgang.title: news.gang
newsgang.subtitle: An AI-assisted media product that compares left, right, and center coverage of the same story and publishes an objective synthesis.
newsgang.description: news.gang is a product concept built around a sharp editorial wedge: instead of aggregating articles, it helps readers detect how ideological framing changes across outlets. The public landing experience positions the product as a transparent, source-linked, human-reviewed AI media layer.
newsgang.outcome: What makes the project interesting is the product design, not just the interface: a free objective layer, a paid comparison layer at €2.99/month, visible source attribution, bilingual positioning, and an editorial workflow designed around curation, framing rewrite, and human review.

bullets.one: Next.js-based product landing experience with bilingual messaging, strong positioning, and conversion-focused information architecture.
bullets.two: Editorial model built around source curation, left/right framing rewrites, and an objective synthesis with transparent links and AI + human bylines.
bullets.three: Subscription concept that separates free fact synthesis from paid ideological comparison, making the monetization logic part of the product itself.

guda.label: Featured Build Case
guda.title: Guda
guda.subtitle: A self-contained artist portfolio CMS built for Pablo Azurza, a contemporary artist from Tolosa.
guda.description: Guda is a full-stack portfolio and content management system I built end-to-end for a working artist. The brief was simple: a clean public-facing website to showcase works and news, plus a private admin panel the artist could operate alone — no agencies, no CMS subscriptions, no tech dependency.
guda.outcome: The result is a fully owned, zero-subscription product. All images stored directly in PostgreSQL, magic link authentication replaces passwords, and the admin panel is a single-page app the artist can use from any device. Deployed and running on Cloudflare infrastructure.

bullets.one: Node.js + Express backend with PostgreSQL storing everything including binary image assets, eliminating the need for a CDN or external storage service.
bullets.two: Magic link email authentication via Resend — no password to remember, no login form to maintain, 15-minute token expiry with SHA-256 hashing.
bullets.three: Vanilla JS admin panel with drag-and-drop reordering, publish/unpublish toggles, and full CRUD for works, news, and biography — all without a JS framework.

hutech.label: Featured Build Case
hutech.title: HuTech Product Studio
hutech.subtitle: Marketing and product website for HuTech's internal incubation studio, where I work as Product lead.
hutech.description: HuTech Product Studio is the product acceleration arm of HuTech Ventures — a venture studio focused on health, robotics, and longevity tech. I built the public-facing site as a content-driven, framework-free product: all copy, case studies, team info, and CTAs live in a validated JSON data layer, not hardcoded in markup.
hutech.outcome: The architecture separates content from presentation deliberately — a JSON Schema validator enforces data quality before any deploy, and client-side JavaScript renders case studies and team sections dynamically from the data layer. Deployed on Cloudflare Workers with Plausible analytics for privacy-first tracking.

bullets.one: Content-driven architecture where all site copy and case studies live in a JSON data layer with JSON Schema validation enforced at build time — no CMS needed.
bullets.two: Cloudflare Workers deployment with a vanilla JS + HTML/CSS stack: zero framework overhead, global edge delivery, and a single wrangler.toml for the full deploy pipeline.
bullets.three: Built as the product lead of the studio itself — the site reflects the Problem → Prototype → MAP framework the team uses internally for 2-month product cycles.

timetracking.label: Featured Build Case
timetracking.title: HuTech Time Tracking
timetracking.subtitle: A full-stack HR and time tracking system built for internal use at HuTech — clock-in, time off, invoices, goals, and payroll exports in one tool.
timetracking.description: HuTech Time Tracking is an internal operations product I built to replace scattered spreadsheets and manual HR processes at HuTech. It covers the full employee lifecycle from daily time logging to quarterly goal evaluation — with both employee self-service views and an admin layer for oversight and payroll exports.
timetracking.outcome: The system handles real business rules: overlap detection on manual entries, CA public holiday enforcement on time-off requests, one PDF per month per employee for invoices, and Google Calendar sync for time-off visibility. Real-time clock state updates via SSE, and all binary assets (PDFs) stored directly in PostgreSQL.

bullets.one: Clock in/out with live timer, manual hour entry with overlap detection, and a week-by-week session view — built on Next.js 15 API routes with SSE for real-time state.
bullets.two: Time off requests with automatic CA public holiday and weekend enforcement, optional one-way Google Calendar sync, and admin oversight across the full team.
bullets.three: Admin layer with monthly hours reports, CSV payroll exports, invoice upload tracking with Resend email alerts, and quarterly goal evaluation per employee.
